summary: Three examples show how caller coordination, layered indirection, and interface obligations can concentrate in a single owner. These candidates demonstrate the report format; they are not findings about your repository.
inspected: Synthetic order intake fixture; no repository evaluation performed.
strengths: A persistence adapter already isolates database details.
Caller-facing error behavior has contract tests worth preserving.
limits: Synthetic example only; source locations and observations illustrate the format.

findings.title: Give order intake one owner
findings.observation: HTTP and batch callers repeat the same validation and pricing decisions.
findings.proposal: Keep intake decisions behind one interface; let callers supply an order and receive its outcome.
findings.benefits: One place to change the rule.
findings.verification: Exercise both callers with invalid input.

before.meaning: Arrows mean calls. Red edges repeat caller-owned coordination.

after.label: Order intake
after.meaning: One caller contract. Validation, pricing, and persistence coordination are internal.

findings.title: Collapse the pass-through pipeline
findings.observation: A request crosses four thin forwarding modules before reaching the behavior tests need.
findings.consequence: A new validation rule requires changing forwarding arguments and several test setups.
findings.proposal: Concentrate the workflow inside intake and verify it through the same interface callers use.
findings.benefits: One place to change the rule.
findings.tradeoffs: Replace forwarding tests only after contract coverage protects their behavior.
findings.verification: Exercise accepted, rejected, and persistence-failure outcomes through intake with a local stand-in.

before.meaning: Top to bottom: request flow. Red bands are forwarding responsibilities.

after.label: Order intake
after.meaning: Private responsibilities stay together; persistence remains substitutable.

findings.adrConflict: Revisits ADR-004: the current forwarding layers add no independent policy. Confirm that constraint still holds before consolidation.

findings.title: Shrink what callers must know
findings.observation: Callers must normalize, validate, price, and save in a specific order.
findings.proposal: Accept an order once and own the sequence and invariants inside intake.
findings.benefits: One place to change the rule.
findings.verification: Exercise both callers with invalid input.

before.label: Behavior hidden today
before.meaning: Qualitative view: a broad caller contract hides little behavior.

after.label: Behavior hidden by intake
after.meaning: Qualitative view: a smaller contract hides the workflow; sizes are not metrics.

recommendation: Start with order intake ownership: it removes repeated caller decisions while preserving the persistence adapter and existing error contracts.
